title: Piksters HydroPik Ultra Water Flosser Set each $49.50 @ Woolworths
body:
Deal: Piksters HydroPik Ultra Water Flosser Set each $49.50 @ Woolworths

[adehmar] Are these useful at all if I floss properly every night?
[zoza] yes, also useful for people who have braces
[BigBook] Yes most studies have found water flossing to be more effective at removing plaque than string flossing.
[spaceflight] For the non believers
Results:
The majority of the studies favored water flossers over dental floss in plaque reduction. Water flosser was also found to be effective in removing plaque from inaccessible interproximal areas of the tooth surfaces as compared to dental floss.
Conclusion:
Based on the scope of this review, results suggest that water flossers can be used as an effective alternative to dental floss in patients with manual dexterity, patients undergoing orthodontic treatment, and patients with dental prostheses.
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10906797/
[BigBook] Thanks for sharing that.
Not sure if the medical consensus on this topic has changed and OzBargain is just behind the times, or if they’re just in denial because they want to justify continuing to use the cheaper option.
[guidedlight] Yes, if you continue flossing with string floss.
I do both. I use the water flosser in my morning shower and the string floss at night.
For me the string flosser mechanically removes plague and food between teeth. The water flosser is great for cleaning the gum line.
I think the word “flosser” is incredibly misleading.
[grain-farmer] I use them (different brand though) after each meal, and string floss at night. They're just much quicker to use.
[Wolfenstein98k] Daily reminder that the primary job of floss is to scrape the faces of the teeth that your brush doesn't reach (imagine the sides of the teeth that face each other), and to get down to the gumline.
This does zero for that.
It dislodges chunks, but so does manual floss.
Just use floss, get to the gumline (GENTLY), and scrape up the sides of those teeth that your brush can't get.
[Doy] I’ve tried to get into the habit of flossing but never successfully. Water flossing is that more accessible bridge that is way better than not doing anything, even if not optimal.
[donman92] Take it easy bro. Some of us aren't as gifted / have it easy as you with flossing and routine. If it helps it helps.
[TightLikeThisx] It can be better than not flossing but it can also be worse than flossing. I've known people who had gum issues from using these things instead of flossing.
Flossing is like tying your shoelaces. Sure it annoying takes up time and is a learned skill but it's worth making it a habit. But at the end of the day you do you.
[donman92] I also have very very tight spaces so flossing is near impossible for me
[TightLikeThisx] @donman92: "Near" impossible.
Some floss are better than others.
Oral B Essential is the only one that will fit between my teeth without getting shredded.
Honestly I hate flossing and looked into these things to avoid it but from what I understood they are not a replacement for flossing. I have a sibling whose gums receded from using a water pick. Ill take the everyday annoyance of flossing over the pain of gum/tooth disease and the dentist bills. If you ignore my warnings then just make sure your dentist is measuring your gumline at your check ups. They use a special tool for this and record it over time to track whether your gums are receding or not. If they do recede you open yourself up to cavities and tooth sensitivity.
[Wolfenstein98k] Put the roll of floss in the way of your toothbrush. Don't make excuses
[donman92] All good mate. That's what my dental checkups are for 😘👌
[chaucolai] I've got wires behind my teeth after braces - so to floss I need a combination of floss and picks for the front. I'm also bad at dental hygiene in general, so.. that level of effort will legitimately never happen. A water flosser is a nice medium shrug
[GunnerMcDagget] It's not perfect, but both have their benefits. Regular floss removes built up stuff on the outside of the teeth, but regular floss doesn't effectively get to the stuff between the teeth close to the gums. Especially if there's an inaccessible cavity that can't be easily dealt with (have one myself). Water flossing is better for that.
Ideally, use both. If that's not an option, use at least one.
[Ozzy Ozbargain] That's where interdental brushes come in
[GunnerMcDagget] Yepp. But water flossing is generally quicker and easier. Especially if the gaps aren't large enough for interdental brushes.
[Maxeyboy18] My brother is a dentist.
You should try and do both, but if he had to pick one, he'd pick a water flosser.
[Wolfenstein98k] Ask your doctor how water removes plaque before it becomes calculus.
[spaceflight] Daily reminder that anyone can make up anything with no facts needed.
But if we look at something that has looked at the facts
Results:
The majority of the studies favored water flossers over dental floss in plaque reduction. Water flosser was also found to be effective in removing plaque from inaccessible interproximal areas of the tooth surfaces as compared to dental floss.
Conclusion:
Based on the scope of this review, results suggest that water flossers can be used as an effective alternative to dental floss in patients with manual dexterity, patients undergoing orthodontic treatment, and patients with dental prostheses.
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10906797/
[Tech45] $10 more on Amazon if that works better for anyone.
[Two50rr] Not all teeth are the same.
Mine were very close and hard to get floss in between.
After normal flossing then using a water flosser right after, you can see the remnants that normal flossing didn't get to. Also normal flossing could get stuff that the water losses doesn't.
[lunartemis] For general household cleaning, this also works well for cleaning the inside of your dishwasher
[Plasma] Has anyone used this model compared to the mini version ?
[reddot12] I had one of these - my experience was not great: it can get messy with water splashing and gums bleeding. There will be some discomfort when doing it as it gets close to the gums, you might feel some weird, painful sensaiton. I'm happy to keep using the dental floss.
[grain-farmer] The splashing and bleeding stops quickly once you're familiar with it, in my experience. Once you get used to it and find the right angles and speed setting (I use higher for my back teeth, lower for the front), it's fine. I can get pain if the water is cold on a certain tooth, but that's because it probably needs a root canal at some stage.
[Luigy] Don't have this model, but been using my waterpik as a mini pressure washer to clean out our yeti bottle lids. It's great at pushing out mold/gunk in the crevices, which can build up surprisingly quickly.
